answer: That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. Because the pearl cap is applied per key at the orchard settlement, the beacon audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. No single identity may earn more than 2622 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 17 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
